title: st.context.theme.type does not trigger a rerun when the theme changes
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

According to [this comment](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5009#issuecomment-2946544937), accessing `st.context.theme.type` in a script should cause the app to automatically rerun when the user changes the theme. This does not happen, the value only updates after a manual rerun.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.write(f"Current theme: `{st.context.theme.type}`")
st.write("Change the theme in Settings — this text should update automatically.")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the script above with `streamlit run app.py`
2. Note the theme value shown
3. Open the Settings menu (☰ → Settings) and switch between Light and Dark theme
4. Observe that the displayed theme value does NOT change
5. Manually click the Rerun button. The value now updates correctly

### Expected Behavior

The app reruns automatically when the theme changes, and `st.context.theme.type `reflects the new value without requiring a manual rerun.


### Current Behavior

No automatic rerun occurs. `st.context.theme.type` keeps returning the old value until the user manually triggers a rerun.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.57.0
- Python version: 3.14.4
- Operating System: Linux (kernel 7.0.0-15-generic)
- Browser: Chrome  148



### Additional Information

_No response_

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15287)

This is a bug report (and partly a known limitation) about `st.context.theme.type` not auto-updating when the user switches the Light/Dark theme via Settings — the value only refreshes after a manual rerun or another widget interaction.

**Likely root cause:** `st.context.theme.type` is populated from `ctx.context_info.color_scheme` in `lib/streamlit/runtime/context.py`, which is set from the `RerunData.color_scheme` field that the frontend sends on `BackMsg` (`getThemeColorScheme()` in `frontend/app/src/App.tsx` ~L1945). When the theme is changed via `setAndSendTheme` / `updateTheme` in `frontend/app/src/util/useThemeManager.ts`, only the local React `activeTheme` state is updated and a `SET_THEME_CONFIG` host message is emitted — no `BackMsg` (rerun) is sent to the backend, so the cached `color_scheme` on the session stays stale until the next user-triggered rerun.

This is the known tradeoff introduced by PR #11870 (which fixed a MPA regression from #11797) and is already documented in the docstring of `st.context.theme` with a pointer to umbrella issue #11920. A targeted fix would be to trigger a rerun (or send an updated `color_scheme` via a `BackMsg`) from `setAndSendTheme` when the active theme's color scheme changes — ideally only when the script actually accesses `st.context.theme` to avoid unnecessary reruns.

### Related Issues

- [#11920 — Make `st.context.theme` work in all situations](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11920): Umbrella issue tracking the known reliability problems with `st.context.theme.type` (first run, MPA, and theme switches). This issue is essentially a concrete report of one of the cases covered there and is likely a duplicate.
- [#11536 — Expose all theming config options in `st.context.theme`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11536): Related feature work on `st.context.theme`; any fix here should ideally generalize to keep all exposed theme fields in sync after a theme change.
- [#5009 — Detect if the app is in Light/Dark mode at runtime](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5009) (closed): Original feature request that led to `st.context.theme.type`; referenced by the reporter and useful context for the intended behavior.
